title: Scope an Azure access and governance plan — worked decisions
explanation:
Azure RBAC assigns a role to a security principal at a scope. Management group, subscription, resource group, and resource scopes form an inheritance hierarchy. Start with the task and smallest useful scope rather than assigning Owner to make an error disappear. Contributor can manage resources but cannot generally assign Azure RBAC roles. Reader can inspect resources without changing them. A management role does not automatically grant every data-plane permission; reading a storage account configuration differs from reading its blobs.

Azure Policy evaluates resource configuration against organizational rules. A policy can audit or deny configurations, but it does not give a user permission to create resources. Resource locks protect against certain management changes and are not a replacement for authorization or backups. An administrator diagnosing a denied operation should examine the identity, effective role assignment, scope, policy result, and locks. Record which control caused the decision before changing access. Use fictional identities and a paper scope diagram before experimenting in an isolated subscription.
distinctions: RBAC controls who can act; Policy evaluates allowed resource configurations.
Management-plane access and data-plane access can require different roles.
lab: Draw a subscription with dev and production resource groups.
Assign a fictional developer resource-management access only to dev; identify who may assign roles.
Add a policy restricting locations and predict a denied deployment despite valid RBAC.
Record two positive and two negative authorization tests.

example.situation: A Contributor can create a VM in one location but receives a policy denial in another.
example.reasoning: RBAC permits the action; a separate location rule constrains the resource.
example.result: Use an allowed location or obtain an approved policy exception, rather than granting Owner.

sources.title: Azure Administrator official certification guide

questions.prompt: A role was assigned at subscription scope, but only dev access was intended. What change reduces excess privilege?
options: Move the assignment to the dev resource group after checking dependencies
Add an identical assignment at tenant scope
Rename the user
Add a cost tag
questions.explanation: Scope limits the set of resources affected by a role assignment.

questions.prompt: A delete action fails although the operator has the required role. A resource has a delete lock. What should be investigated?
options: The browser language
Whether Reader would grant more permissions
The billing currency
The lock and its approved removal process
questions.explanation: Locks and RBAC are separate management controls; identify the actual cause before changing either.

title: Separate Azure durability, access, and recovery — worked decisions
explanation:
An Azure storage design has several independent decisions: the data service, redundancy, access control, network reachability, and recovery policy. Locally redundant storage maintains copies within a location, while zone-redundant storage spreads copies across availability zones in the primary region. Availability and service support vary, so verify the selected region and account capabilities before deployment. Replication is not the same as a backup: an authorized deletion or bad overwrite may be replicated too.

Blob versioning and soft delete can help recover from supported deletion or overwrite scenarios when configured in advance. Retention choices determine the recovery window and cost. A private endpoint gives a service a private network interface, but clients still need working DNS and authorization. Disabling public access without a tested private path can break legitimate clients. A useful acceptance test reads a permitted object, rejects an unauthorized identity, resolves the expected endpoint, and restores a deliberately modified test object. Keep recovery evidence and remove temporary objects after the exercise.
distinctions: Replication helps durability and availability; recovery settings address supported deletion scenarios.
A private network path does not replace authentication and authorization.
lab: Create a paper storage design for zone failure and accidental overwrite.
Choose a redundancy approach and a separate retention/versioning policy.
Trace a client through DNS, private endpoint, and data authorization.
Write a restore test with original content, changed content, and an expected recovered version.

example.situation: An application reaches a private endpoint but cannot read a blob.
example.reasoning: Network reachability does not establish data authorization.
example.result: Inspect the application identity and blob permissions before broadening network exposure.

questions.prompt: A team plans to disable public storage networking. Which validation should precede the change?
options: Test client DNS, private routing, and authorized data access
Only rename the account
Remove identity roles to simplify testing
Assume private DNS works automatically in every network
questions.explanation: Private endpoint success depends on the actual client path and DNS design.

questions.prompt: A restore operation reports success. What provides stronger evidence of application recovery?
options: Check only the storage account name
Delete the recovery log
Assume redundancy guarantees the desired version
Read the restored test object and compare expected content
questions.explanation: Successful operation status alone does not prove the restored content is the required version.

title: Trace an Azure application failure — worked decisions
explanation:
Troubleshooting a cloud application starts with the failing conversation, not a random restart. Identify source, destination, protocol, port, and name resolution. Azure network security groups evaluate rules using priority; lower numeric values have higher priority. Check effective rules at relevant interfaces and subnets as well as routes and service configuration. An open rule does not create a listener, and a healthy VM power state does not prove an application is serving requests.

Azure Monitor metrics summarize numeric measurements over time. Logs provide records that can be queried and correlated, when collection has been configured. The Activity Log helps investigate management-plane events such as a configuration change; it is not a complete record of every application request. An alert needs a condition, evaluation settings, and a useful response destination such as an action group. Compare an observed failure to a known baseline and validate both the symptom and telemetry after a targeted correction. Avoid opening all inbound ports as a diagnostic shortcut.
distinctions: A network allow rule does not start an application listener.
Activity Log management events differ from application request logs.
lab: Draw a client, subnet, VM, and HTTPS service with port 443.
Write conflicting NSG rules with priorities 100 and 200 and predict the matching decision.
Build a failure timeline with one management change and one application symptom.
Define an alert condition, recipient, and a test proving the alert works.

example.situation: A VM is running, but HTTPS fails after a network-rule update.
example.reasoning: Power state does not establish end-to-end service availability.
example.result: Compare effective rules, the route, and the listener; verify an actual HTTPS request after repair.

sources.title: Azure Administrator official certification guide

questions.prompt: HTTPS fails after an NSG change while the VM remains running. Which evidence best narrows the cause?
options: Effective rules, routing, and a listener check for the failing path
Only CPU model information
A successful ping from an unrelated network
The subscription display name
questions.explanation: Follow the actual source-destination conversation and its dependencies.

questions.prompt: The Activity Log shows no configuration changes during an application error. What follows?
options: The application could not have failed
All user requests succeeded
No further evidence can exist
Application logs and other telemetry are still needed
questions.explanation: Management activity is not a complete record of application behavior.

title: Design AWS temporary access and trust — worked decisions
explanation:
AWS IAM policies describe allowed or denied actions on resources, sometimes with conditions. The effective decision depends on applicable policies and evaluation rules; an explicit deny overrides an allow. A role has a trust policy describing who may assume it and permission policies describing what the resulting session may do. These are different questions. A workload should normally use a suitable role and temporary credentials rather than a long-lived access key embedded in application code.

For cross-account access, examine both sides of the relationship and the applicable resource policy or role-assumption design. An allow statement in one place does not guarantee end-to-end authorization. Encryption adds another dependency: reading an object encrypted with a customer managed KMS key may require permission to use that key as well as permission to read the object. Test with the actual workload identity and record denied actions. Do not resolve errors by adding wildcard administrator access; narrow the missing permission or incorrect trust relationship and retest the intended operation.
distinctions: Role trust determines who can assume a role; permissions determine what its session can do.
Data access and KMS key access can be separate dependencies.
lab: Draw a fictional workload role and a single permitted S3 bucket.
Write a task-to-permission table and identify who can assume the role.
Add an encrypted object and document the additional key-access dependency.
Predict an allowed read, denied write, and explicitly denied read.

example.situation: A role can read ordinary objects but cannot read a KMS-encrypted object.
example.reasoning: Object permission alone may not authorize use of the encryption key.
example.result: Inspect KMS permissions and key policy alongside the S3 permission.

sources.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate official certification guide

questions.prompt: A role has the required S3 policy, but an external account cannot assume it. Which part needs inspection?
options: The role trust and caller assumption permissions
Only the S3 storage class
The billing contact name
The application logo
questions.explanation: Session permissions cannot help until the caller can legitimately assume the role.

questions.prompt: A developer fixes an AccessDenied error by attaching administrator access. What is the better lasting correction?
options: Embed the new credentials permanently
Disable encryption on every bucket
Remove all logging
Identify the denied action and grant only the necessary scope
questions.explanation: Use the failure evidence to correct narrowly scoped authorization and verify the intended task.

title: Design for failures across availability zones — worked decisions
explanation:
A resilient application must tolerate failures in each dependency, not just duplicate its web servers. An Application Load Balancer can distribute requests to healthy targets across configured availability zones. An Auto Scaling group can replace unhealthy capacity, but the application should avoid keeping essential session state only on a replaceable instance. Externalize state in a suitable shared service and make request handling resilient to retries.

Database availability and read scaling are different needs. A conventional RDS Multi-AZ DB instance deployment uses a standby for failover rather than as a read replica. Other RDS deployment types have different capabilities, so identify the actual product and deployment model. A queue can decouple producers and consumers, allowing work to wait during a temporary processing disruption. Consumers should handle possible redelivery and use idempotent processing where required. Define recovery time and acceptable data loss, then test a component failure. A diagram with two icons is insufficient evidence that the application still works when one dependency disappears.
distinctions: High availability and read scaling solve different problems.
Queue redelivery requires safe consumer behavior, not an assumption of exactly-once business effects.
lab: Draw two availability zones, a load balancer, replaceable app instances, and a database.
Identify all session state and remove single-instance dependencies on paper.
Add a queue and define how duplicate message processing will be detected.
Walk through losing one zone and record expected user-visible behavior.

example.situation: Web instances span two zones, but carts exist only in local process memory.
example.reasoning: Replacing a failed instance loses its users’ carts.
example.result: Move required session state to an appropriate shared service and test recovery.

sources.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate official certification guide

questions.prompt: A multi-zone web tier loses user carts during instance replacement. Which dependency was overlooked?
options: Session state stored on individual instances
The count of region names
The DNS record comment
The cost allocation tag
questions.explanation: Compute redundancy alone does not preserve local state.

questions.prompt: A failover test restores service in twelve minutes, but the target is five. What should the team conclude?
options: Two zones guarantee the target regardless of test results
The target refers only to backup size
The test should be discarded
The tested design misses the recovery-time target
questions.explanation: Measured recovery must be compared with the required recovery objective.

title: Match AWS storage to access and recovery needs — worked decisions
explanation:
Storage selection starts with how an application accesses data. S3 provides object storage, EBS provides block volumes for supported compute use cases, and EFS provides a shared file system. An application expecting file-system operations cannot always be moved to an object API without changes. Durability, access latency, sharing, capacity, and recovery requirements all matter. A low storage price alone does not establish the lowest total cost.

Lifecycle transitions can move eligible objects to different storage classes, but retrieval patterns, minimum storage duration charges, and restore latency must be considered. Some archive classes require a restore before data can be read. Backups and versioning address recovery scenarios distinct from ordinary replication. Document the required recovery point and recovery time, then verify a sample restore. Transfer, requests, and retrieval charges may dominate a rarely accessed dataset that is unexpectedly read in bulk. Use a workload estimate and current pricing rather than assuming every archival class is interchangeable. A paper design is sufficient for this introductory exercise; no paid resources are required.
distinctions: Object, block, and file storage expose different interfaces.
Low stored-byte cost does not imply low retrieval cost or immediate access.
lab: Classify an image archive, a VM disk, and a shared Linux directory by access interface.
Write retrieval frequency and maximum acceptable recovery time for each.
Compare immediate access with delayed archive restoration for the image archive.
Estimate storage, requests, retrieval, and transfer categories without creating resources.

example.situation: An archive must support immediate incident retrieval, but the proposed class requires a restore delay.
example.reasoning: The storage price is lower but the access requirement is not met.
example.result: Select an appropriate access class or revise the recovery requirement explicitly.

sources.title: AWS Solutions Architect Associate official certification guide

questions.prompt: A program requires block-device semantics for its instance disk. Why is S3 not a drop-in replacement?
options: Object API operations differ from block-device operations
S3 has no durability
S3 can only store text
EBS is an identity service
questions.explanation: Storage interfaces affect how applications read, write, and manage data.

questions.prompt: A backup exists, but nobody has tested reading restored data. What remains unproven?
options: Whether the backup has a name
Whether a cost tag can be added
Whether a region has a console
Whether the restore meets content and recovery-time requirements
questions.explanation: Backup existence is weaker evidence than a validated restore.

title: Distinguish identity, verification, and authorization — worked decisions
explanation:
An identity identifies a person, workload, or device. Authentication establishes confidence in that identity; authorization determines what it may access. Microsoft Entra ID is a cloud identity service. Multifactor authentication combines suitable factors and reduces risks from a stolen password, but it does not replace appropriate access permissions or protect every possible session compromise. Single sign-on reduces repeated sign-ins across supported applications without removing the need for access decisions.

Conditional Access evaluates signals and applies access controls according to policy. A policy might require stronger authentication for a sensitive application or restrict access based on device conditions. These decisions require deliberate scoping, licensing awareness, and testing. Zero Trust principles include verifying explicitly, using least privilege, and assuming breach; a corporate network location alone is not sufficient trust. For a beginner exercise, create a fictional access matrix and test normal, elevated-risk, and emergency-access scenarios on paper. The objective is to explain the decision path, not to configure a live tenant or risk locking out an administrator.
distinctions: Authentication establishes identity; authorization grants access.
Single sign-on reduces repeated prompts but does not grant every application permission.
lab: List fictional staff, contractor, and workload identities.
Build an application access matrix with the minimum required privileges.
Write normal and risky sign-in scenarios and choose verification requirements.
Document how policy testing avoids locking out emergency access.

example.situation: A contractor signs in successfully but cannot open a finance application.
example.reasoning: Authentication succeeded; application authorization may still be absent.
example.result: Verify the intended assignment rather than treating all successful sign-ins as universal access.

sources.title: Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals official certification guide

questions.prompt: A contractor can sign in but cannot use the finance app. What should be checked?
options: The intended application authorization and assignment
Whether successful authentication must bypass policy
Only the browser theme
The office printer queue
questions.explanation: An authenticated identity still requires the appropriate resource access.

questions.prompt: A policy change may affect every administrator. What is an appropriate rollout approach?
options: Apply broadly with no recovery plan
Remove all monitoring first
Share one permanent password
Test scope and emergency-access behavior before broad enforcement
questions.explanation: Access controls require validation so a misconfiguration does not prevent legitimate recovery.

title: Choose threat protection by the evidence needed — worked decisions
explanation:
Security products address different evidence and response needs. Microsoft Defender capabilities cover areas such as endpoints, email, identities, and cloud workloads. Extended detection and response correlates signals across supported security domains. Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud-native SIEM and SOAR platform that can collect and analyze data from multiple sources and support response workflows. The name of a product alone does not mean that every source is connected or every response is enabled.

An alert is a signal to investigate, while an incident can group related activity for analysis and response. A good analyst asks what telemetry supports the hypothesis, how timestamps and entities relate, and what evidence is missing. Automation should have appropriate permissions and escalation boundaries. Blocking an account can contain harm but also interrupt legitimate work, so response actions need context and authority. In this introductory exercise, use invented events and classify them by source. Write a short investigation that separates confirmed actions from uncertain conclusions and identifies the next useful evidence.
distinctions: SIEM centralizes and analyzes logs; endpoint protection acts on endpoint threats.
An alert is evidence to investigate, not automatic proof of compromise.
lab: Create fictional email, endpoint, and identity alerts for one user.
Normalize times and identify which signals refer to the same device or session.
Assign evidence sources to an investigation and write one benign alternative.
Define a response action with an owner, authority, and verification step.

example.situation: A suspicious email and an endpoint alert reference the same user within minutes.
example.reasoning: Correlation strengthens an investigation but still needs entity and time validation.
example.result: Inspect linked evidence before declaring the scope or automating disruptive containment.

sources.title: Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals official certification guide

questions.prompt: Two alerts share a username but have inconsistent time zones. What should be done first?
options: Normalize timestamps and validate linked entities
Declare a confirmed sequence immediately
Delete one alert
Ignore every identity signal
questions.explanation: Reliable correlation depends on comparable times and identity context.

questions.prompt: Sentinel is enabled but a required data source is not connected. What is the consequence?
options: All its events are automatically available anyway
Every endpoint is isolated
The source stops generating events
That source can remain a visibility gap
questions.explanation: Product deployment does not prove telemetry ingestion or detection coverage.

title: Separate classification, retention, and leakage prevention — worked decisions
explanation:
Data protection begins by understanding what data exists and how it should be handled. Sensitivity labels can classify content and, when configured, apply protection such as encryption or access restrictions. The label name alone does not prove a particular protection setting. Data loss prevention policies can identify sensitive content and apply actions to risky handling across supported locations. A policy must be scoped and tested so legitimate work is not unnecessarily disrupted.

Retention controls govern how long content is kept or when it is deleted. They solve a different problem from preventing an inappropriate share. Investigation and legal processes may impose additional preservation requirements, so a user deleting a file does not necessarily determine whether all retained copies disappear. Use fictional documents for a tabletop exercise: classify a public announcement, an internal plan, and a payroll sheet, then define sharing and retention behavior separately. Record the intended policy outcome and a test for a false positive. Regulatory requirements must be established by the organization; a training classification is not a legal compliance determination.
distinctions: Sensitivity, DLP, and retention answer different handling questions.
A label name is not evidence that encryption is configured.
lab: Create fictional public, internal, and payroll document descriptions.
Assign a sensitivity category and permitted recipients for each.
Write a DLP action for an external payroll share and a separate retention rule.
Test an authorized exception and a false-positive case on paper.

example.situation: A document is labeled Confidential, but external access still works.
example.reasoning: The label may not be configured with the assumed enforcement.
example.result: Inspect actual label protection and sharing policies instead of relying on its name.

sources.title: Security, Compliance, and Identity Fundamentals official certification guide

questions.prompt: An external share succeeds despite a Confidential label. What should be inspected?
options: Configured label protection and applicable sharing policies
Only the file icon
Only the document title
The user monitor size
questions.explanation: Names do not prove technical enforcement.

questions.prompt: A team wants to prevent leakage and keep records for an approved period. What design fits?
options: Use a longer password as the only control
Assume retention blocks all sharing
Assume DLP sets every retention period
Define both handling restrictions and retention rules
questions.explanation: Preservation and inappropriate disclosure are different requirements.

title: Connect cloud choices to business outcomes — worked decisions
explanation:
Cloud transformation is a business change supported by technology, not simply moving the same machines elsewhere. Define the outcome first: shorter release cycles, improved resilience, flexible capacity, or better access to data. Infrastructure as a service leaves more operating-system and application responsibilities with the customer. Managed platforms can reduce some operational work, while software as a service offers an application with a different control and responsibility boundary. Every model still requires appropriate customer decisions about data and access.

Elastic capacity can follow variable demand, but it does not guarantee lower cost. Idle resources, data transfer, inefficient software, and duplicated systems can increase spending. A total-cost comparison includes migration, operations, staff effort, and ongoing usage. Some workloads may remain on premises because of dependencies or requirements; hybrid designs introduce their own connectivity and management needs. Use a small fictional organization and compare alternatives against measurable goals. Avoid selecting services only because they are newer. State tradeoffs and identify what evidence would change the recommendation.
distinctions: Elasticity changes capacity with demand; it does not guarantee savings.
A managed service changes responsibilities rather than removing all customer responsibility.
lab: Choose a fictional shop with seasonal traffic and a slow release process.
Define two measurable business goals and a dependency constraint.
Compare keeping servers, using managed hosting, and using a hosted application.
List cost categories and define how the chosen outcome will be measured.

example.situation: A company moves idle servers to cloud VMs and its bill increases.
example.reasoning: Migration alone did not right-size resources or change operating practices.
example.result: Measure utilization and redesign capacity against the business need.

sources.title: Google Cloud Digital Leader official certification guide

questions.prompt: Cloud spending rises after unchanged idle servers are migrated. What is the most useful next step?
options: Measure utilization and right-size the design
Assume all cloud services are free
Add more idle replicas immediately
Remove cost visibility
questions.explanation: Lift-and-shift does not automatically optimize resources or operations.

questions.prompt: A workload depends on a local device with a strict latency requirement. What should influence the migration plan?
options: Only the marketing category
Only the billing contact
Only the number of developers
The dependency and measured latency constraints
questions.explanation: Architecture must meet actual workload requirements, potentially including hybrid operation.

title: Choose data and AI approaches responsibly — worked decisions
explanation:
Data projects begin with a question and trustworthy information. An analytical warehouse supports large-scale analysis, while a transactional application database is designed around operational reads and writes. BigQuery is Google Cloud's managed analytics warehouse; selecting it does not by itself fix missing, biased, duplicated, or poorly governed data. Identify source quality, ownership, access rights, and update needs before drawing conclusions from a dashboard.

Machine learning learns patterns from examples, while generative AI produces content based on learned patterns and context. Generated text can be plausible but incorrect. Evaluate a system against representative tasks and define human review where consequences require it. A baseline without AI may be simpler and more reliable for some problems. Avoid training and evaluating on the same examples when the goal is generalization. Protect sensitive information, consider who is represented in the data, and monitor results after deployment. An introductory tabletop can compare a sales dashboard, a prediction task, and a drafting assistant without uploading any real customer data.
distinctions: Analytics reports on data; predictive and generative tasks need their own evaluation.
Fluent generated output is not evidence of factual correctness.
lab: Describe a sales-reporting task, a demand-prediction task, and a drafting task.
Choose an approach for each and name the required data.
Create five fictional evaluation cases including a failure or underrepresented case.
Define accuracy evidence, privacy boundaries, and a human-review trigger.

example.situation: A generated support response sounds confident but invents a product feature.
example.reasoning: Fluency is not a correctness check.
example.result: Validate against an approved knowledge source and require review for unsupported claims.

sources.title: Google Cloud Digital Leader official certification guide

questions.prompt: An assistant invents a product capability. Which response improves reliability?
options: Check approved references and route unsupported claims for review
Publish because the prose is confident
Remove all evaluation cases
Use real secrets as prompts
questions.explanation: Correctness requires evidence and appropriate review.

questions.prompt: A rule-based process already solves a narrow task accurately. What should an AI proposal demonstrate?
options: That AI is mandatory for every task
Only a longer model name
That evaluation is unnecessary
A measurable benefit against that baseline
questions.explanation: A simpler baseline is a useful comparison for cost, reliability, and benefit.

title: Plan Google Cloud responsibility and reliability — worked decisions
explanation:
Cloud providers secure parts of the underlying platform, but customers retain responsibilities that depend on the service. Identity permissions, data handling, and application configuration remain central. IAM roles should match actual duties at appropriate scopes, and identities used by workloads need deliberate permissions too. Do not equate provider infrastructure security with a correctly secured application. Logging and monitoring must provide evidence relevant to the service's operation.

Reliability is a measurable service property. A service-level indicator is a measurement such as successful request proportion. A service-level objective is a target for that measurement, while an agreement can define contractual commitments. A backup addresses recovery but is not equivalent to automatic high availability. Design around the business impact of interruptions and data loss, and test recovery rather than assuming it. Cost governance includes ownership, budgets, and reviewing usage; a budget notification should not be treated as a universal hard spending cap. Use fictional figures and a paper service plan for this beginner lab.
distinctions: An SLI measures behavior; an SLO sets a target.
Budget notifications are not a universal automatic spending limit.
lab: Draw provider and customer responsibility columns for a managed application.
Define a successful-request indicator and a target.
Write a backup restore test and distinguish it from automatic failover.
Assign a cost owner and an action to take when a budget notification arrives.

example.situation: A team receives a budget notification and assumes all spending has stopped.
example.reasoning: A notification is not a universal hard cap.
example.result: Inspect usage and apply the intended cost-control actions explicitly.

sources.title: Google Cloud Digital Leader official certification guide

questions.prompt: A Google Cloud budget notification is delivered. What should the owner assume?
options: Usage must be reviewed; notification alone is not a universal spending cap
All billable resources have necessarily stopped
Every charge is invalid
The project is automatically deleted
questions.explanation: Budget alerts support cost management; actions must match the actual configuration.

questions.prompt: A service has backups but no redundant serving capacity. What is unproven?
options: Whether data can have a name
Whether users can be assigned roles
Whether a project has an owner
Automatic continuity during a serving failure
questions.explanation: Backups support recovery; availability requires an appropriate serving design.

title: Read the Terraform change workflow — worked decisions
explanation:
Terraform describes desired infrastructure in configuration and uses providers to interact with platform APIs. A provider implements resource and data-source operations. A resource represents something Terraform manages; a data source reads information for use in configuration. Initialization prepares the working directory and required providers or modules. Validation checks configuration consistency, but it does not establish that a proposed infrastructure change is safe or permitted by a remote API.

A plan compares configuration, state, and observed information to propose actions. Review creates, updates, replacements, and destroys before applying. A replacement can interrupt service even if the resource name remains familiar. A saved plan can preserve the reviewed proposal, but still requires secure handling and a suitable execution workflow. Apply makes changes and can incur costs or remove resources. For this introductory exercise use only the local provider and disposable files, or a paper plan; no cloud account is required. Observe how changing an input affects the plan, then compare the resulting file to the requested configuration.
distinctions: Validate checks configuration; plan proposes infrastructure actions.
A resource manages an object; a data source reads information.
lab: Create a disposable directory or use a paper local_file example.
Describe a local file resource with a filename and harmless content; identify its provider.
Predict init, validate, plan, and apply outcomes before running anything.
Change only the content and compare the planned action with the resulting file.

example.situation: A valid configuration proposes replacing a resource that stores required state.
example.reasoning: Syntax validity does not establish acceptable operational impact.
example.result: Review the replacement and recovery requirements before applying.

sources.title: Terraform Associate official certification guide

questions.prompt: A reviewed plan includes replacement of a data-bearing resource. What should happen before apply?
options: Assess disruption and recovery requirements
Ignore replacement because syntax is valid
Delete every backup
Assume names prevent data loss
questions.explanation: Replacement is a material lifecycle action requiring impact review.

questions.prompt: A beginner wants to learn Terraform without cloud charges. Which exercise fits?
options: Deploy a large paid cluster by default
Store production credentials in configuration
Run destroy against a shared workspace
Manage a harmless disposable local file with the local provider
questions.explanation: A local-only example teaches the workflow without creating cloud infrastructure.

title: Protect Terraform state and coordinate changes — worked decisions
explanation:
Terraform state maps configuration addresses to managed objects and records information needed for subsequent operations. It can contain sensitive values. Marking an output sensitive suppresses ordinary display but is not a guarantee that the value is absent from state. Protect state access and storage, and avoid committing state or secrets to a source repository. Configuration belongs in version control; state needs its own controlled handling.

A backend determines where state is stored and may provide locking depending on its type and configuration. Locking helps prevent concurrent operations from corrupting coordination, but it does not replace review or permissions. A remote backend does not automatically make all data secure. Confirm encryption, access, recovery, and supported lock behavior. If an operation is interrupted, establish whether it is still running before considering lock recovery. Force-unlocking another active operation can create conflicting writes. For a tabletop exercise, model two operators trying to change the same workspace, and explain how ownership, serialization, and recovery evidence prevent accidental conflicts.
distinctions: Sensitive display suppression is different from excluding secrets from state.
Remote storage and locking depend on backend capabilities and configuration.
lab: Draw two operators sharing one infrastructure workspace.
List data that state may contain and who should access it.
Write a sequence where one apply holds a lock while another waits.
Describe how to investigate an interrupted operation without unlocking an active writer.

example.situation: A sensitive output is hidden in console output, so a developer proposes committing the state file.
example.reasoning: Suppressed display does not mean the state excludes the value.
example.result: Keep state in a controlled backend and review secret exposure separately.

sources.title: Terraform Associate official certification guide

questions.prompt: A teammate wants to commit tfstate because sensitive outputs are hidden. What is the correction?
options: State can still contain secrets and needs controlled storage
Hidden outputs guarantee a secret-free file
Rename the extension to make it safe
Publish it only during working hours
questions.explanation: Display behavior does not protect the underlying state contents.

questions.prompt: A backend is remote. What still needs verification?
options: Nothing; remote means automatically secure
Only the resource color
Only the project slogan
Access control, protection, recovery, and locking behavior
questions.explanation: Backend capabilities and configuration determine actual security and coordination.

title: Build reusable Terraform inputs and outputs — worked decisions
explanation:
A Terraform module groups configuration into a reusable unit. Input variables define values supplied by a caller, while outputs expose selected results. Clear variable types and validation rules help catch unintended values before changes are applied. A module should have an understandable contract rather than requiring callers to inspect every internal resource. Provider requirements and version constraints help communicate compatibility.

The dependency lock file records selected provider versions and checksums. It is not the same as Terraform state, and it does not lock every remote module version. Choose module version constraints deliberately and review upgrades. Resource relationships can often be inferred from references; explicit depends_on is useful for dependencies that are not otherwise expressed, but unnecessary broad dependencies can reduce parallelism and obscure intent. Count and for_each create multiple instances with different addressing behavior. Stable keys help avoid unintended address changes when a collection evolves. Use a disposable local module to observe input, output, and addressing changes before applying these ideas to real infrastructure.
distinctions: Inputs configure a module; outputs expose selected results.
The provider dependency lock file is not Terraform state or a universal module lock.
lab: Sketch a local-file module with a filename input and a path output.
Add a type and a validation rule for an allowed label.
Compare numeric count addresses with for_each keys for a changing set.
Write an upgrade checklist covering provider selection and module constraints.

title: Use Linux ownership and permissions deliberately — worked decisions
explanation:

Read, write, and execute have context-specific meaning: execute on a directory allows traversal, while read allows listing its entries. A process may need traversal permission on every parent directory before it can open a file. Avoid changing everything to mode 777 to hide an access problem.

Use commands such as id, ls -l, and namei -l to inspect the actor and path. chmod changes mode bits, while chown changes ownership. A umask influences permission bits removed from the defaults used when creating new objects; it does not retroactively rewrite existing files. Additional security controls can still deny access when ordinary mode bits look correct. RHCSA is a practical exam, so explain and perform tasks in a disposable Linux VM and verify results as a non-root test user. Work only inside a dedicated lab directory and retain a way to restore the starting state.

title: Verify Linux services now and after reboot — worked decisions
explanation:

Enabling alone does not necessarily start it immediately, and starting alone does not guarantee startup after reboot. Inspect the unit with systemctl status and relevant properties, and review logs with journalctl for the service. Use a harmless existing service in a disposable VM rather than changing a production host.

Troubleshooting follows evidence. A failed service may have a syntax error, missing file, occupied port, wrong permissions, or unmet dependency. Check the specific error before changing security policy. A listening socket does not prove that a remote client has a permitted network path, and a firewall opening does not create a listener. Verify the service locally, then test the intended client path. For exam-style practice, make the required state persistent and reboot the disposable VM to confirm it. Keep notes describing the observed failure and the exact change that corrected it.

title: Plan persistent Linux mounts and storage verification — worked decisions
explanation:
Linux storage involves several layers: a block device or logical volume, a file system, a mount point, and mount configuration. Formatting creates a file system and can destroy existing contents, so the introductory exercise should use a disposable VM disk or a paper plan, never an unidentified host disk. lsblk and blkid help inspect devices, file systems, and identifiers. A directory existing does not prove that the intended file system is mounted there; inspect mount information and capacity.

A temporary mount may disappear after reboot unless startup configuration establishes it. Entries in /etc/fstab can identify file systems by UUID, avoiding assumptions that a device name will always be assigned the same way. Incorrect entries can disrupt startup, so preserve the original file, validate syntax and mount behavior, and retain VM recovery access. Logical volume growth and file-system growth are separate steps whose commands depend on the file system. Do not assume all file systems support shrinking. The practical goal is to verify the correct backing storage, read/write behavior, and persistence after a controlled reboot.
